notes.title: The town square
notes.text: A 300 m square rotated 10° clockwise from north. The courthouse and Lyric remain whole inside the plot.

notes.title: Measured terrain
notes.text: The ground is the real ground: bare-earth elevations from the 2018 USGS 3DEP lidar flight, drawn at true scale with no exaggeration. The plot falls 15.2 m from the courthouse ridge to its lowest corner (143–158 m above sea level). Contour lines are one metre apart, heavier every five; the cut edges of the plot show the profile. Use Contours to hide the lines.

notes.title: Measured roofs and heights
notes.text: All 62 buildings carry measured roofs. Flat facets were fitted to the lidar returns over each OpenStreetMap footprint, so parapets, roof steps, pitches and rooftop plant are the surveyed ones, and each wall rises to the eave the lidar saw. Roof colours are sampled from the USDA NAIP aerial photograph. The lidar was aligned to the map by a 1.8 m shift.

notes.title: Surveyed trees
notes.text: The 91 trees stand where the lidar canopy shows them, with their surveyed heights and crown widths, including the courthouse lawn. Species, leaf colour and blossom are illustrative.

notes.title: Façades from photographs
notes.text: Read from dated photographs on Wikimedia Commons: the Thompson House (cream, three storeys, roofed gallery round the corner), Trustmark and Bouré beside it, FNB’s white-columned porch and shutters, Neilson’s pavement canopy, the south-east block as five separate fronts (Village Tailor, Hinton & Hinton, A C’s, Off Square Books with its diamond panels, The Frame Up), Square Books’ terracotta paint, the Lyric’s white front and brick sides, and the marble monument south of the courthouse. The west-side canopies and the Grillehouse gallery come from one aerial view and are approximate. Other fronts keep generic period detail.

notes.title: Measured and illustrative
notes.text: Measured: building outlines, streets, paths and shop names (OpenStreetMap); ground, building heights, roof forms and tree positions (USGS lidar, 2018); roof colours (NAIP). Interpreted: wall colours, windows, storefronts, awnings, fronts not covered by a photograph, planters, benches, parking bays, people, traffic, weather and festival layouts. Buildings altered since 2018 keep their 2018 shape.

notes.title: Courthouse study
notes.text: The custom model includes paired porticoes, arcaded bases, and a domed clock cupola. The mapped outline supplies the plan; unmeasured proportions are interpreted.

notes.title: Books and music
notes.text: Mapped shop names identify the commercial streets. Storefronts and the Lyric model are simplified interpretations. Shop listings reflect OpenStreetMap and may be outdated.

notes.title: Explore the wider campus
notes.text: Use the campus-wide atlas for searchable main-campus buildings, playing fields, and streets beyond the miniature.

notes.title: Architectural detail pass
notes.text: Façades now distinguish arched and sash windows, stone lintels, cornices, gallery railings, column orders, and roof forms. Main elevations were compared with photographs. Minor dimensions and unseen elevations remain interpreted.

notes.title: Street life and wind
notes.text: Moving traffic, parked vehicles, bicycles, crowds, wind, and small façade projections are illustrative. Cars occupy mapped lanes and parking; extra festival crowds use open ground and closed roads. Gameday crowds gather in the Grove and Circle. These are atmospheric scenes rather than an attendance or parking survey.

notes.title: Ground materials
notes.text: Pavements, lawn and asphalt are drawn as materials with scored joints, and the slopes are shaded from the measured terrain. The courthouse grounds (lawn, walks, iron fence, shrub and flower beds, benches, lamps), the parking courts and the planted medians follow the aerial image and photographs; their exact dimensions, planting and furniture are approximate.

note.text: The Double Decker Arts Festival brings music, art, and food to the Square.
